item.title: Who’s behind the new ‘stealth model’ Ox Alpha?
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ha
item.description: A mysterious new AI model called Ox Alpha has driven certain corners of the internet into a frenzy of speculation.

item.title: Uber faces fine of nearly $1B over automated driver suspensions
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ha
item.description: The Dutch Data Protection Authority is fining Uber €825 million in the second largest penalty issued under Europe’s GDPR.

item.title: Linkdaze’s smart calendar is built to run a household, not just track a schedule
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: Linkdaze's smart digital calendar stands out for not putting its features behind a paywall, including an AI meal planner tool.

item.title: TechCrunch Mobility: The custom chip driving Waymo’s robotaxi ambitions
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility — your central hub for news and insights on the future of transportation.

item.title: Flock CEO calls for ‘compromise’ as surveillance company faces growing backlash
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ha
item.description: Flock Safety faces a growing public outcry over concerns that its surveillance technology could be misused.

item.title: Is it legal to train AI models on copyrighted books? It’s complicated
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: Most published authors have, without their knowledge or consent, contributed to the development of the same AI tools that threaten to undermine their livelihoods. That seems illegal, right?

item.title: Two years after launch, Walmart’s Flipkart is closing in on India’s quick-commerce leaders
item.dc:creator: Jagmeet Singh
item.description: Flipkart's quick-commerce venture is delivering 1.1 million to 1.2 million orders a day, nearly triple its November volume.

item.title: Harvard’s $699 startup bootcamp offers AI avatars of its instructors
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ha
item.description: In the HBS Foundry program, AI avatars provide feedback during practice pitches and board meetings.

item.title: Will the DOJ’s investigation into a16z spook other VCs?
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ha
item.description: On the latest episode of Equity, we wonder why the DOJ is investigating startup board seats.

item.title: Inherent, founded by DeepMind alumni, says its AI ‘teammate’ just outperformed Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating research
item.dc:creator: Anna Heim
item.description: Built by DeepMind alumni, British AI lab Inherent released Faraday, an AI agent whose ability to replicate scientific papers could be a stepping stone for innovation.

item.title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ha
item.description: OpenAI is calling for California to strengthen SB 53, an AI safety bill that the company previously opposed.

item.title: Frontier AI labs still won’t say how they’d contain a rogue model
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: A new study finds leading AI labs have few publicly documented plans for containing rogue models, raising questions about preparedness as AI systems increasingly demonstrate unexpected and potentially dangerous behavior.

item.title: US battery startups have found a lifeline in defense
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: U.S. battery startups pulled in $500 million in grants from the Department of Energy, throwing a lifeline to an industry that was on the ropes after EV incentives were slashed.

item.title: Pixel 11 Pro XL review: Snappier cameras can’t hide an iterative upgrade
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Google’s Pixel 11 Pro XL brings snappier cameras and genuinely useful AI features like Rambler, but its iterative upgrades may not be enough to tempt recent Pixel owners.

item.title: Michael Polansky is training an AI model on skin that’s still alive
item.dc:creator: Connie Loizos
item.description: Michael Polansky — better known publicly as Lady Gaga's partner and a former top deputy to Sean Parker — has quietly spent years building an AI-driven startup that keeps living human skin tissue alive for weeks outside the body to discover new skincare compounds, and is only now going public about it.

item.title: Japanese space tech startup Letara expands beyond satellite thrusters with $16M
item.dc:creator: Kate Park
item.description: Japanese space startup Letara is betting its hybrid rocket technology can move beyond small satellite thrusters into a broader market for space, defense and security, after raising ¥2.6 billion ($16 million).

item.title: Anthropic’s Opus 4.6 is a smut-machine
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: Anthropic forbids its Claude models from generating sexually explicit content. But a series of tests conducted by TechCrunch found that it didn't take much to get past the restriction.

item.title: Nvidia partners with data center developer Cloverleaf
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Nvidia continues to pour money into data center development — just as AI data centers bring lots of money into Nvidia.

item.title: How AI accounting startup Rillet raised $100M and became a unicorn in 48 hours
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: Rillet CEO Nicolas Kopp shared growth numbers at a board meeting and set off a fundraising frenzy from Iconiq, Sequoia and others. Without even trying.

item.title: Apple is reportedly cutting hundreds of jobs from Siri, Vision Pro teams
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Apple has admitted that some roles are being impacted as it shifts its focus away from certain initiatives.
